scope: Software engineering roles at Salesforce, not Salesforce-platform implementation roles at unrelated employers

records.title: MTS hiring drive: technical passes, resume deep dive rejection
records.datePrecision: Month stated in report title; exact interview/publication day unavailable
records.sourceType: First-person community report (named author: Tharun Vemula)
reportedRounds: OA: timestamp-window counting and partition-cost optimization.
Virtual screening revisited OA reasoning and Merge Intervals.
DSA: weighted job scheduling, moving from recursion to DP and binary search.
DSA + LLD: task-dependency queries and a Ludo class design.
Hiring manager: resume and project discussion; author reports technical hire feedback but manager no-hire and overall rejection.
records.takeaway: Resume fluency can decide the outcome after strong coding. Prepare an LLD fallback even when the anticipated MTS loop is coding-heavy.
records.rehearsalPrompt: In 90 seconds, explain one resume project: customer problem, your ownership, architecture, one trade-off, measured outcome. Then defend every noun you used.
records.caveat: Self-reported, independently unverified. Unexpected LLD occurred in this candidate's drive; it does not establish the format for another team.

records.title: MTS Bangalore: coding-heavy onsite and an offer
records.role: MTS / software engineer; author reports 3 years' experience
records.datePrecision: Onsite day explicitly stated in report body; OA date reported as 2026-05-15
reportedRounds: HackerRank OA and virtual screening.
Two one-hour onsite DSA rounds: permutation counting, repeated array-sum reduction using a heap, randomized-set operations, and Coin Change II.
A 30-40 minute hiring-manager conversation covered work problems, project decisions, and behavior.
Author explicitly reports no dedicated LLD/HLD round in this MTS pool drive and says they accepted an offer.
records.takeaway: Practice explaining and implementing two problems under a clock, then switch cleanly into a concise work-story discussion.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Explain the invariant and complexity before coding a heap problem. Dry-run duplicates and boundary inputs; leave five minutes for validation.
records.caveat: Anonymous anecdote. Absence of design here conflicts with other MTS reports, so do not remove design prep. The author's claimed randomized-set implementation is not validated.

records.title: AMTS Bangalore: CS fundamentals and a small-system design
records.role: AMTS / Associate Member of Technical Staff
records.datePrecision: Month stated in title; exact interview/publication day unavailable
reportedRounds: A 100-minute OA with bit-operation, array-update, and tree-diameter problems.
Technical round: project architecture, linked-list intersection, distinct islands, and C++/OOP fundamentals.
Design conversation: library-management entities, relational data, a filtering request structure, and concurrent trending-book counts.
Author reports selection.
records.takeaway: Even an early-career loop can assess how you connect entities, APIs, storage, and concurrency. Refresh the language fundamentals on your resume.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Design a library checkout flow in six minutes. State entities, API input/output, one database invariant, and how you prevent conflicting concurrent updates.
records.caveat: Anonymous, unverified report for a specific AMTS position. Its C++ topics are evidence from this candidate, not a universal language requirement.

records.title: San Francisco: coding screens and a conversational final round
records.role: Software engineering; exact level not stated
records.datePrecision: Onsite date explicitly stated; post reports an offer on February 2, 2026
reportedRounds: OA followed by a manager conversation combining background and technical problem solving.
Two engineer interviews included binary search/sorting and a modulo-based encoding problem.
A roughly 90-minute onsite with an engineering leader mixed behavioral discussion and real team engineering problems. The candidate reports receiving an offer.
records.takeaway: Practice switching from code to an engineering conversation: clarify the real problem, explain assumptions, compare alternatives, and defend one decision.
records.rehearsalPrompt: In 90 seconds, explain a production incident you worked on. Then spend five minutes answering how you diagnosed it, what you changed, and what you would monitor next.
records.caveat: Anonymous and independently unverified. Exact role level and team are not stated; this final-round format is not a promise for another San Francisco role.

records.title: SMTS: whiteboard metrics design and music-service LLD
records.location: Not stated; an in-office round is reported
records.datePrecision: First round explicitly described as the first week of December 2025; later onsite day unspecified
reportedRounds: First round combined behavior questions with enumeration of weekly work-hour strings that meet a target sum.
In-office whiteboard round: a metrics-collection system HLD and music-service class diagrams.
Follow-ups included password-storage knowledge.
Author reports rejection and reflects that their system-design answers lacked practical depth.
records.takeaway: Practice operational explanations: data volume, ingestion, aggregation, retention, failure modes, and security. Diagrams need defensible reasoning.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Explain a metrics pipeline in eight minutes. Pick a write path, quantify load, and defend how you handle backpressure, duplicates, retention, and an unavailable downstream service.
records.caveat: Self-assessment does not prove why the employer rejected the candidate. Location and exact onsite date are not supplied.

records.title: LMTS backend: connection pool and distributed-systems depth
records.role: LMTS / Lead Software Engineer, Backend / Distributed Systems; author reports approximately 10.3 years' experience
records.datePrecision: Month stated in title; exact interview/publication day unavailable
reportedRounds: 75-minute OA with heap and DP/sorting reasoning.
Virtual DSA included stack implementations and a project challenge.
LLD asked for a connection pool with acquisition, return/close, bounded capacity, timeout, and concurrent callers.
In-person HLD: marketing campaigns with distributed transactions, scaling, failure recovery, and saga discussion.
Manager round deeply explored current architecture, leadership, and mentoring. Author reports an offer.
records.takeaway: Use a drawing to establish shared understanding, state concurrency invariants, and make implementation trade-offs explicit before moving on.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Design a bounded connection pool. Narrate its lifecycle, timeout behavior, double-return protection, and concurrent access, then explain a deliberate time-versus-complexity trade-off.
records.caveat: Lead-level India anecdote; its depth and format should not be assumed for every level. The candidate's complexity claims and concurrency implementation were not independently verified.

records.title: LMTS: job scheduling and a zero-downtime cache migration
records.datePrecision: Month stated in title; exact interview/publication day unavailable
reportedRounds: 75-minute OA and DSA involving array queries/reordering.
Job-scheduler LLD covered creation, persistence, dispatch, and execution.
HLD addressed migration from Memcached to Redis with consistency, fallback, and rollout.
An 80-minute manager round reportedly mixed a deletion-tolerant palindrome, distributed priority queue, and ownership/collaboration discussion.
Author reports receiving and declining an offer.
records.takeaway: Design answers should cover rollout, observability, consistency, and rollback, alongside the steady-state architecture.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Pitch a zero-downtime cache migration in seven minutes. Define success metrics, compare transition strategies, explain stale-read risks, and specify rollback triggers.
records.caveat: Anonymous lead-level anecdote. The post's broad statement about final interviews being in-house is not sufficient to establish a company-wide rule.

records.title: Official: narrate decisions and demonstrate collaboration
reportedRounds: The guidance describes technical and behavioral conversations with engineers and a hiring manager, often including whiteboard work.
It explicitly recommends asking clarifying questions, thinking aloud, explaining decisions, and preparing examples of individual and team strengths.
It also describes adapting to panel changes and preparing questions for interviewers.
records.takeaway: Make the reasoning visible: clarify, propose, compare, implement, validate, and connect decisions to requirements.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Ask a mock interviewer to interrupt with a new constraint. Restate the change, revise your approach, and explain why the revision meets it.
records.caveat: An undated learning module describes a general process; exact panel size, whiteboard format, and ordering may differ from the candidate's current recruiter-confirmed loop.

records.title: Official: rehearse STAR stories and engage thoughtfully
records.datePrecision: Official article publication date explicitly shown as 2025-08-13; reviewed 2026-10-10
reportedRounds: General candidate guidance rather than a round-by-round experience.
Match preparation to the job description, rehearse your delivery, organize experiences with STAR, and demonstrate a learning mindset when receiving feedback.
Prepare informed questions about the role, team, and AI.
records.takeaway: Prepare short stories with a specific personal action and a verifiable outcome; rehearse aloud until they sound conversational.
records.rehearsalPrompt: Answer 'Tell me about a disagreement' in two minutes using situation, task, action, and result. Follow with what you changed afterward.
records.caveat: General official advice, not a guaranteed engineering interview rubric. The article also says AI use during interviews requires a specific interviewer prompt and asks candidates not to record or transcribe interviews.

editorialNotes: Dates on anecdotes are reported interview dates, not asserted publication dates.
Community reports are self-reported and independently unverified; use them as practice prompts, not forecasts or verified company policy.
Coverage is weighted toward India because recent detailed accessible reports are from India. No team names were supplied in the selected reports.
Exclude the April 2026 Reddit eight-round post from premium curated content: placeholder location and promotional guide link reduce editorial confidence.
Avoid universal round counts, guaranteed question claims, unverified OA cut-offs, compensation promises, and source authors' unverified algorithm-complexity claims.
